doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Jazz history in Japan and growing up after the war
summary: Early Japanese jazz and Shanghai, his generation's rock tastes, and the postwar generation's lack of war memory; his father's view that the army was crazy.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. I read the history of jazz in Japan. They, in the book, said even before World War I, already Japanese jazz singers existed. And at that time they went to Shanghai. Because Shanghai was a colony of England, or something like that.
Yeah, so there is an English jazz band.
That’s right, in fact a fellow named Buck Clayton played in Shanghai like in the 30’s. Do you know Eiji Kitamura?
He told a very interesting story about some of the musicians heard it over the radio, the United States radio. But the military had their own radio stations and they would hear it from that source.
But my generation is always rock music. Not much jazz. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
So you were born ten years after the end of World War II. And is there any, in your experience growing up, what was the memory of World War II. Did it influence your life at all?

No, no. After ten years I mean no more after war era. No more after war era. It’s kind of a different generation. I don’t have any idea about the war or anything. So Americans means rock star or movie star.
Not as the enemy or anything.
Right. Okay. But your parents didn’t talk about it too much?

My father didn’t went to war. He is an instructor for a glider, the airplane, in Japan. And mostly Japanese people knew Japanese Army was crazy. Because nobody thought who had the mind, nobody thought that we were able to win, generally in Japan. But nobody said, because if you said it the military came to you and you’d go to jail.
So that’s why people thought the Army was crazy you know.
They thought the Army was crazy for engaging in such a thing.
Yeah, and such a long time you know.
